Title: Harden SECURITY DEFINER / mutable-search_path RPCs (Supabase advisor)
Description:
## Problem

The Supabase security advisor (`function_search_path_mutable`) flagged \~113 functions on project `zkwcbyxiwklihegjhuql` (count per the 2026-06-01 advisor scan — **re-confirm live before sizing**). Functions that are `SECURITY DEFINER` **and** have a role-mutable `search_path` are a privilege-escalation surface: a caller who can influence `search_path` can shadow built-in objects and have the definer-privileged function execute attacker-controlled code.

Split out of AUTH-011 ([SAN-367](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-367/auth-011-production-auth-checklist)) as standalone hardening — it is **not** a launch blocker for the auth checklist, but should be burned down before/just after MVP.

## Scope

* Re-run the advisor to get the **current** list + count:
  * Supabase advisor `get_advisors(type: "security")` → filter `function_search_path_mutable`.
  * Cross-check which of those are `SECURITY DEFINER` (highest risk first).
* For each flagged function, pin the search path: `ALTER FUNCTION <fn>(<args>) SET search_path = '';` (and schema-qualify all references inside the body), or `SET search_path = public, pg_temp` where empty is impractical.
* Prefer `SECURITY INVOKER` for any function that does not genuinely need definer rights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Advisor re-run produces the authoritative list (replace the \~113 estimate with the real number).
- [ ] Every `SECURITY DEFINER` function has a fixed `search_path`.
- [ ] `function_search_path_mutable` warnings = 0 in a fresh `get_advisors(type: "security")`.
- [ ] No RLS regression: spot-check that hardened RPCs still return correct rows for an authed user and 0 for an impostor (same probe used in AUTH-011 RLS verification).
- [ ] Migration applied via `apply_migration` (versioned, in repo).

## Context

* Driver: AUTH-011 production auth audit ([SAN-367](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-367/auth-011-production-auth-checklist)), 2026-06-02.
* Related advisor item: leaked-password protection is a dashboard toggle, tracked separately on [SAN-367](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-367/auth-011-production-auth-checklist)'s config checklist — not part of this issue.
